messages:
Jordan: Heads up — Liz (customer) just hit back-to-back 429s after we flipped the staged rate-policy rollout this morning. She sent a repro curl and a perf timeline.
Jordan: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"input": "test"}'
# returns 429 with body: {"error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 3}
```
Jordan: They run a fairly bursty integration test (many parallel short requests). They used a single API key for all tests.
Mira: I can see a spike correlated with the rollout window in traces — lots of small requests from that key hitting the rate limiter and exhausting the token bucket. 429 percent went from ~0.2% -> 3.4% in the 5m window.
Ana: Canary config note: we bumped rl-policy v2 to staged_percent=12 at 09:00 UTC (targeting low-volume customers). The policy uses per-key TB (token_bucket) with burst=50 and refill_rate=10/s.
Mira: That burst setting is too low for their workload pattern. With many concurrent short calls they deplete instantly then clients retry and backoff isn't ideal -> saw sawtooth.
Sam: Wanted: quick mitigation plan so customer can continue tests. Options: 1) temporary partner exemption, 2) reduce staged_percent (pause rollout), 3) rollback to rl-v1. Which is fastest?
Ana: Reducing staged_percent to 0 for the canary group is the fastest toggle via feature flags. No code deploy. I can flip.
Jordan: Meanwhile CS asks if we can offer a temporary quota bump to Liz’s org to unblock them.
Mira: Agreed: pause rollout first so new traffic won't get rl-v2. Then we can analyze proper burst/refill config.
Jordan: Repro notes I asked Liz for: exact curl rate (rps), number of parallels, client library version, and whether they used connection keepalive. She said 40 parallel clients at ~6rps each for 15s bursts.
Mira: That explains it — aggregate ~240rps in bursts. Given per-key burst 50 the bucket drains in <1s. Then retry storms cause 429s.
Ana: I'll flip the staged_percent to 0 now. Action: update feature-flag rollout.rate_policy.rl_v2.canary_percent=0 and push config.
Ana: @deploy-bot kicking config push...
deploy-bot: config-push: feature rollout change submitted by Ana at 2024-05-12T09:14:55Z.
deploy-bot: config-apply: succeeded for service=ingress-policy-evaluator env=prod.
Ana: Change applied — staged_percent is now 0.
Sam: I'll watch 429 rate and token-bucket saturation metrics. Which dashboards to follow?
Mira: Watch: rl.429_rate by policy, ingress.token_bucket_fill (per-key), and svc.gateway.retries. Also grep traces for "rate_limit_exceeded". I ran a quick Prom query:
```
sum(rate(rl_rate_limit_exceeded_total[1m])) by (policy)
```
Mira: Immediately after flip 429 rate dropped from 3.4% -> 0.4% in the canary cohort. Looks like pause worked.
Jordan: Good. I'll tell Liz we paused the rollout and offer a temporary quota increase for their API key while we tune. She prefers not to change anything client-side right now.
Jordan: Plan for next steps: 1) Mira to propose new token_bucket params (burst + refill) or switch to per-connection smoothing. 2) Ana to stage a smaller canary (3%) with updated settings. 3) Run synthetic replay to validate. 4) CS to coordinate customer window.
Mira: Proposed quick patch: burst=600, refill_rate=120/s for Partner-tier keys + smoothing window 5s. Also add a per-key queue limiter to damp retries. I'll run a local sim with their workload shape.
Ana: If Mira's sim looks good, we'll stage canary at 3% to a curated cohort (exclude known-bursty customers). We'll also enable header-based traffic classification so Partner/test keys can get the higher burst.
Sam: I'll create an alert that fires if canary 429 rate >1% sustained for 3m and ping #eng-oncall. Also add a dashboard row to the canary health panel.
Jordan: CS: I'll tell Liz we paused the rollout, we'll give them a temporary +5000 token bump for the next 2 hours, and we'll coordinate a re-run after the tuned canary.
Jordan: Filing support ticket ST-49321 with reproduction details + action taken.
Mira: Quick notes for postmortem: - rollout gating diff logs missed because rollout metric didn't include per-key burst patterns. - need better pre-rollout sim harness. - add an automated canary smoke test that mimics parallel bursty clients.
Ana: I'll add a checklist item to the rollout runbook: "simulate extreme-parallel bursts for keys with known shared-key patterns".
Jordan: Customer update sent. Liz replied: :thumbsup: thanks, that should help.
Sam: Closing actions: Mira runs sim and posts config suggestion, Ana stages new canary once suggestion approved, Jordan handles customer scheduling, Sam watches alerts.
Mira: I'll post sim results within 2h.
Ana: I'll leave the staged_percent at 0 until we get sims.
Jordan: Thanks team. Follow-up thread if anything flares. :white_check_mark:
